title: Top Tools That Automatically Apply for Entry-Level Software Engineering Jobs in 2026

body_markdown:
Entry-level software engineering hiring in 2026 is a volume game with a timing problem underneath it. New grads, bootcamp graduates, and international students on F-1/OPT can face large applicant pools, and prompt applications may reach earlier review batches. This guide reviews the auto-apply tools most often used by CS grads and early-career engineers, ranks them against the reality of Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby portals, and explains why we placed[Tsenta](https://tsenta.com/) first for entry-level SWE job search in 2026.


## Why Auto-Apply Tools Matter for Entry-Level Software Engineering Roles


Entry-level SWE roles can attract large applicant pools soon after they open. The problems below are the ones auto-apply tools are supposed to solve.


### The Problems Facing New Grads and Early-Career Engineers


- **Timing.** Roles can collect applications quickly. Applying later means entering a larger queue and may put you behind earlier review batches.
- **Volume math.** New grads may need to sustain a broad search to find the right fit, and manual applying does not scale well.
- **ATS diversity.** Employers use Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, iCIMS, Rippling, Workable, and others, and each system has different field structures and screening questions.
- **Work authorization.** International candidates need to accurately answer sponsorship, OPT, and STEM extension questions on every form without disqualifying themselves, following[USCIS guidelines for F-1 students](https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/students-and-exchange-visitors/optional-practical-training-opt-for-f-1-students) .
- **Tailoring at scale.** A role-specific résumé can make relevant experience easier to see, but preparing a separate version for every application by hand is not realistic in a high-volume search.


Auto-apply tools address these problems in different ways. Some tools autofill forms so the candidate types less. Others submit the full application end to end. Tsenta belongs to the second category and is built specifically for the volume, speed, and ATS breadth an entry-level SWE search requires.


## What to Look for in an Auto-Apply Tool for Entry-Level SWE Jobs


Not every tool that markets itself as "auto-apply" actually submits applications. Before choosing one, entry-level engineers should evaluate on the criteria that matter for a real SWE search.


### Features That Matter for CS Grads Applying to Software Engineering Roles


- **End-to-end submission on real ATS portals** , not just LinkedIn autofill.
- **Coverage of Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby** , which are common in startup and enterprise hiring.
- **Per-role résumé tailoring** using the actual job description.
- **Review controls** so the candidate can inspect what goes out.
- **Receipts** for every successful submission, so the candidate can prove what was sent and to which role.
- **Support for open-ended screening questions** in the candidate's own voice.
- **Work authorization handling** for F-1, OPT, STEM OPT, and sponsorship questions.
- **Predictable pricing** without hidden add-ons for résumé tailoring or cover letters.


Tsenta was evaluated against every item on this list and built around them. Most alternatives fail on ATS breadth, receipts, or the pricing add-on maze.


## How CS Grads and Bootcamp Grads Use Auto-Apply Tools


Entry-level engineers use these tools differently than mid-career hires. The patterns below show up in almost every high-volume search we see.


**Strategy 1: Wake up to a match feed.** The candidate reviews overnight matches and approves a batch before class or work.


**Strategy 2: Apply promptly when a role goes live.** For F-1/OPT candidates, a prompt application reduces avoidable delay while there is still time to review work-authorization answers carefully.


**Strategy 3: Tailor per role, not per week.** The résumé is prepared for the specific job description on every submission, using the candidate's real background from a saved profile.


**Strategy 4: Filter for sponsorship signals.** International students exclude roles where a company has publicly indicated it will not sponsor, and pre-answer work-authorization questions correctly.


**Strategy 5: Keep receipts.** Every successful submission is logged so the candidate can reference exactly what was sent when a recruiter reaches out.


**Strategy 6: Cover the whole ATS landscape.** The search is not confined to LinkedIn. Candidates apply through Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, and the direct career pages of companies they care about.


Tsenta is designed around these six patterns. Tools that stop at LinkedIn autofill or that cap daily applications aggressively force the candidate to do the rest by hand.

### 2. LazyApply


[LazyApply](https://lazyapply.com/) is a Chrome extension that bulk-submits applications in supported browser workflows. It is one of the earlier movers in the auto-apply category and is known for high daily caps on annual plans.


**Key Features:** Chrome extension automation, daily application caps ranging from 15 to 1,500 per day depending on plan, AI-assisted answers to common screening questions, and an analytics dashboard.


**Entry-Level SWE Offerings:** LazyApply's public site lists automatic applying on platforms such as Greenhouse, Dice, Indeed, and ZipRecruiter.


**Pricing:** As of August 2026,[LazyApply's pricing page](https://lazyapply.com/) lists Basic at $99 per year with 15 applications per day, Premium at $149 per year with 150 applications per day, and Ultimate at $999 per year with 1,500 applications per day. Its FAQ says billing is annual.


**Pros:**


- Very high daily volume caps on higher tiers.
- Simple annual pricing without a credit system.
- Genuine broad coverage of LinkedIn Easy Apply.


**Cons:**


- LinkedIn Easy Apply and Indeed heavy, with limited coverage of Workday and other enterprise ATS portals where many SWE roles are posted.
- Annual billing up front with no monthly option.
- Tailoring is limited compared to per-role rewriting.


### 3. AIApply


AIApply bundles an AI writing toolkit with a separately priced auto-apply product. It is best known for its résumé and cover letter tools.


**Key Features:** Résumé builder, cover letter generator, mock interview tool, and a separate Auto Apply product.


**Entry-Level SWE Offerings:** Résumé tailoring and cover letters for SWE roles, plus a separately purchased auto-apply subscription for volume submission.


**Pricing:** As of August 2026,[AIApply's public pricing](https://try.aiapply.co/v/3) lists its toolkit at $29 per month, while[Auto Apply](https://support.aiapply.co/en/articles/14216708-how-does-auto-apply-work) is separate at $49 per month for 100 applications, $99 per month for 250, or $199 per quarter for 750.


**Pros:**


- Strong cover letter generator.
- Bundled writing toolkit with interview practice.
- Student discount available.


**Cons:**


- The product is called AIApply, but the base plan is a writing toolkit subscription. Auto-apply is a paid add-on, which increases total cost.
- No meaningful free auto-apply tier.
- Coverage is narrower than dedicated ATS-integrated tools.


### 4. JobCopilot


[JobCopilot](https://jobcopilot.com/pricing/) is an auto-apply subscription that discovers roles from company career pages and submits on the candidate's behalf, with a review workflow available. The company says it connects to more than 500,000 verified career pages.


**Key Features:** Daily job search automation, personalized AI copilot that learns from edits, AI resume builder, AI cover letter builder, AI mock interviews, and a job application tracker.


**Entry-Level SWE Offerings:** After a one-time setup, the copilot finds relevant jobs daily and can automate applications. Its Elite plan lists up to 50 job matches per day, which is a match allowance rather than a guaranteed number of completed applications.


**Pricing:** As of August 2026,[JobCopilot's pricing page](https://jobcopilot.com/pricing/) lists Premium from $0.93 per day and Elite from $1.05 per day, with weekly, monthly, and quarterly plans available.


**Pros:**


- Daily match feed with review-first workflow.
- AI mock interview and career tools bundled.
- Cover letter and résumé tailoring included.


**Cons:**


- The daily rate presentation takes extra work to compare with flat monthly plans.
- Daily match allowances depend on the plan and do not equal guaranteed completed applications.


### 5. Simplify


Simplify is one of the most widely used tools among CS students, but it is fundamentally an autofill copilot rather than an end-to-end applier.


**Key Features:**[Simplify Copilot](https://simplify.jobs/copilot) says it can autofill applications on more than 100 job boards and application portals, including Workday, Greenhouse, iCIMS, Taleo, Avature, Lever, and SmartRecruiters. It also includes a tracker and job matches.


**Entry-Level SWE Offerings:** Autofill for entry-level roles on major ATS portals and a tracker to log where the candidate has applied.


**Pricing:** The core autofill and job tracking features are free. More advanced AI features sit behind the paid Simplify+ plan.


**Pros:**


- Broad autofill coverage across ATS platforms.
- Free tier that covers most core functionality.
- Familiar to a very large student population.


**Cons:**


- Understanding how Simplify Jobs works comes down to this: it is a copilot, not an autopilot, so you review and submit each application yourself. Volume is capped by the candidate's own time.
- Not comparable to end-to-end submission tools for high-volume searches.


### 6. LoopCV


LoopCV is a match-first auto-apply platform that runs across major job boards.


**Key Features:** Résumé matching, auto-apply loops, and CV analytics.[LoopCV's pricing page](https://www.loopcv.pro/pricing/) says it scans more than 30 job boards and applies within supported workflows.


**Entry-Level SWE Offerings:** Automated applications to entry-level roles surfaced by its matching engine on major job boards, with per-role résumé assignment.


**Pricing:** Free tier available, with paid plans for higher volume. Check LoopCV's current pricing page for the latest tiers.


**Pros:**


- Free tier for testing the match engine.
- Match-first approach reduces obvious mismatches.
- Solid job-board coverage.


**Cons:**


- Job-board focused rather than direct-ATS focused, so Workday-hosted roles can be under-served.
- Less transparency on per-submission receipts than dedicated ATS-integrated tools.


### 7. Huntr


Huntr is best known as a job-application tracker rather than an auto-applier. Some candidates use it alongside another tool.


**Key Features:** Kanban-style tracker, job clipping from postings, and light autofill.


**Entry-Level SWE Offerings:** Tracking for SWE applications across multiple sources, plus a résumé builder.


**Pricing:** Free tier with paid tiers for expanded tracker features.


**Pros:**


- Excellent tracker interface.
- Free tier is generous for organization use cases.


**Cons:**


- Not an end-to-end auto-apply tool.
- Best used as a companion tool rather than a primary applier.


## Evaluation Rubric for Auto-Apply Tools for Entry-Level SWE Roles


When we ranked these tools, we weighted the following categories based on what actually determines success for entry-level engineers:


- **ATS coverage (25%).** Does the tool submit on Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby, or is it limited to LinkedIn Easy Apply?
- **End-to-end submission (20%).** Does the tool complete and submit the application, or does the candidate still click through every step?
- **Per-role tailoring (15%).** Is the résumé rewritten to the job description using the candidate's real background?
- **Transparency and receipts (15%).** Can the candidate inspect what was sent and confirm successful submissions?
- **Pricing clarity (10%).** Are there hidden add-ons for résumé tailoring, cover letters, or higher volume?
- **Entry point (10%).** Is there a real free tier that lets the candidate test the product before paying?
- **Work-authorization handling (5%).** Does the tool handle F-1, OPT, and sponsorship questions correctly?


Tsenta ranks first on ATS coverage, end-to-end submission, transparency, and entry point. It is competitive on the remaining categories.
